metadata.description: Code generation tasks for WordPress Interactivity API APIs

tests.prompt: Implement a function that initializes the 'wpbp/store' Interactivity API state with a count of 2 and returns the store state from WordPress.
tests.expected_behavior: `wpbp_gb_interactivity_api_001()` uses `wp_interactivity_state()` for the `wpbp/store` namespace and returns the state array reported by WordPress. Runtime validation confirms the requested `count` value is present without replacing unrelated state that was already registered for the same namespace.
requirements: Use the WordPress Interactivity API state helper
Use the store namespace 'wpbp/store'
Return the final state array

required_patterns.description: Sets the requested count state key

assertions.code: if ( ! function_exists( 'wpbp_gb_interactivity_api_001' ) ) { return false; } $state = wpbp_gb_interactivity_api_001(); return is_array( $state ) && 2 === ( $state['count'] ?? null ) && 'Preserved' === ( $state['label'] ?? null );
assertions.description: The wpbp/store state contains the new count and preserves existing keys

tests.reference_solution: function wpbp_gb_interactivity_api_001(): array { wp_interactivity_state( 'wpbp/store', array( 'count' => 2 ) ); return wp_interactivity_state( 'wpbp/store' ); }

tests.prompt: Implement a function that returns server-processed markup for one interactive element where two independent plugins toggle the same class suffix using unique Interactivity API directive IDs.
tests.expected_behavior: `wpbp_gb_interactivity_api_004()` uses WordPress 6.9 unique directive ID syntax with `data-wp-class` directives on a single element, registers true state flags, and processes the markup through `wp_interactivity_process_directives()`. Use triple-dash unique IDs for both class directives
Return the markup after WordPress processes the directives

tests.prompt: Implement a function that renders the server-side markup of a disclosure button for the 'wpbp/binder' Interactivity API store. It is given the button's label, whether the control is disabled, whether the panel it controls is expanded, an item count and a completion ratio. Return processed markup containing a single <button> whose disabled attribute, aria-expanded attribute, data-count attribute, data-ratio attribute and visible text are all produced by the Interactivity API's server-side directive processing from store state, so the client can keep updating them after hydration.
tests.expected_behavior: The function puts the five values in `wp_interactivity_state( 'wpbp/binder', ... )`, writes a `data-wp-interactive` region containing a BUTTON with `data-wp-bind--disabled`, `data-wp-bind--aria-expanded`, `data-wp-bind--data-count`, `data-wp-bind--data-ratio` and `data-wp-text`, and returns `wp_interactivity_process_directives()`. WordPress removes a bound attribute whose value is `false` unless the attribute is an `aria-`/`data-` attribute, where it renders the string `"true"`/`"false"` instead, and in 7.1 formats a bound number with the JSON encoder, so a float renders as the client would receive it rather than as a PHP string cast.
requirements: Use the 'wpbp/binder' store namespace
Keep the supplied values in Interactivity API state and bind the attributes and the text with directives instead of writing resolved values into the markup
Return the markup after WordPress has processed the directives on the server

required_patterns.description: Binds the button text with a directive

tests.prompt: Implement a function that server-renders a list for the supplied Interactivity API store namespace. Given a list whose entries are the item labels themselves as plain strings, register that list as store state and return processed markup for a <ul> region in which a <template> carrying the Interactivity API list directive has produced one <li> per item, each rendering its own entry as text. WordPress must do the repetition during server-side directive processing rather than the function looping in PHP; a list WordPress cannot repeat on the server must leave the template alone.
tests.expected_behavior:
The function stores the list under the supplied namespace and processes markup shaped as `
`. WordPress appends one copy of the template's inner markup per item after the template's closer, tagging each top-level element with `data-wp-each-child` set to `NS::state.items`. An associative array is skipped because the client would receive it as an object, so the template is emitted unchanged with no generated children.
requirements: Register the items as Interactivity API state under the supplied store namespace
Let WordPress expand the list during server-side directive processing instead of looping in PHP
Render each entry's own string value as the text of its list item
Return the processed markup

required_patterns.description: Uses a template element for the list
Renders each item's label with a directive

tests.prompt: Implement a function that registers a derived greeting for the 'wpbp/ctx' Interactivity API store and returns the supplied markup after server-side directive processing. The greeting is the word Hello, a space, the name found in the local context of the element that is rendering it, and an exclamation mark. An element whose local context carries no name greets the name nobody. Sibling elements with different local contexts must therefore render different greetings from the one registered value.
tests.expected_behavior: The derived value is a PHP Closure stored with `wp_interactivity_state( 'wpbp/ctx', ... )`. During directive processing the closure reads the element's own context with `wp_interactivity_get_context()`, which returns the current context for the namespace on the stack, so the same `state.greeting` reference resolves differently on each element. Precomputing a single string, or reading the context outside the closure, produces the same greeting everywhere.
requirements: Use the 'wpbp/ctx' store namespace
Register the greeting as derived state backed by a PHP closure
Read the rendering element's local context from inside the closure
Return the supplied markup after WordPress has processed its directives

required_patterns.description: Uses a closure for the derived value

tests.prompt: Implement a function that renders the server-side markup of a to-do list wrapper for the 'wpbp/klass' Interactivity API store. Given the number of items in the list and whether the list is pinned, return processed markup for one <div> that always keeps the base class wpbp-list, carries the class wpbp-pinned exactly while the list is pinned, and carries the class wpbp-empty exactly while the item count is zero. Both conditional classes must be decided by the Interactivity API's server-side directive processing from store state, so the client can recompute them after hydration.
tests.expected_behavior: The function stores the count and the pinned flag with `wp_interactivity_state( 'wpbp/klass', ... )` and emits a `data-wp-interactive` region whose DIV carries `data-wp-class--wpbp-pinned` and `data-wp-class--wpbp-empty` directives, then returns `wp_interactivity_process_directives()`. WordPress adds a class when the referenced value is truthy and removes it otherwise, so the empty-state class is expressed by negating the count reference with a leading `!` (or by a derived boolean); the base class is untouched.
requirements: Use the 'wpbp/klass' store namespace
Decide both conditional classes with Interactivity API class directives rather than composing the class attribute in PHP
Keep the base class on the element
Return the markup after WordPress has processed the directives on the server

tests.prompt: Implement a function that contributes a plugin's settings to the shared 'wpbp/merge' Interactivity API store. The supplied settings belong under the store's settings key. Anything another plugin has already registered for that store, including keys nested inside settings, must survive unless the supplied settings replace it, and the function returns the store's resulting state.
tests.expected_behavior: The function calls `wp_interactivity_state( 'wpbp/merge', array( 'settings' => $settings ) )` and returns its result. WordPress merges the new data into the existing state with `array_replace_recursive()`, so nested keys the caller did not mention (such as `settings.labels.open`) survive while the ones it did mention are replaced. Reading the state and writing back a shallow `array_merge()` drops the untouched nested keys.
requirements: Use the 'wpbp/merge' store namespace
Place the supplied settings under the store's settings key
Preserve state that other code already registered, including nested keys
Return the resulting state array

required_patterns.description: Uses the Interactivity API state helper

tests.prompt: Implement a function that renders the server-side markup of a progress bar for the 'wpbp/style' Interactivity API store. The element carries the class wpbp-bar and a hand-written inline declaration of position:relative that must survive. Its inline width and its inline background colour must both be produced by the Interactivity API's server-side directive processing from store state, so the client can keep them in sync. When the supplied colour is null the finished style attribute must carry no background colour declaration at all.
tests.expected_behavior: The function stores the width and colour with `wp_interactivity_state( 'wpbp/style', ... )` and emits a DIV with `style="position:relative;"`, `data-wp-style--width` and `data-wp-style--background-color` inside a `data-wp-interactive` region. WordPress merges each style property into the existing attribute value, keeping declarations it does not manage, and drops a property whose reference resolves to a falsy value, so a null colour removes the declaration rather than writing an empty one.
requirements: Use the 'wpbp/style' store namespace
Write position:relative directly in the element's style attribute
Set the width and background colour with Interactivity API style directives rather than composing the style attribute in PHP
Return the markup after WordPress has processed the directives on the server

tests.prompt: Implement a function that renders a nested Interactivity API region for the 'wpbp/nested' store. The outer element declares the store and a local context holding a card object with the supplied title and the supplied outer theme. Inside it sits a nested element that sets only the card's theme to the supplied inner theme in its own local context: it must not restate the card title and must not declare the store again, relying on the store it inherits from its ancestor. Return the processed markup containing exactly four <span> elements whose text comes from the local context, in this order: the card theme as seen directly inside the outer element, then the card title and the card theme as seen inside the nested element, then the card theme as seen again after the nested element has closed.
tests.expected_behavior: The outer element carries `data-wp-interactive="wpbp/nested"` and a `data-wp-context` value; the nested element carries only a `data-wp-context` with the theme. WordPress merges a nested context into the inherited one with `array_replace_recursive()`, so the title survives inside the nested element, and pops the context when the element closes, so the fourth span shows the outer theme again. The namespace on the stack is inherited by the nested element, so its text directives resolve without repeating `data-wp-interactive`.
requirements: Use the 'wpbp/nested' store namespace and declare it only once, on the outer element
Give the nested element a local context that names only the card theme
Render the four values with Interactivity API text directives reading the local context
Return the markup after WordPress has processed the directives on the server
